newsitem.title: FRANCE: More French property sales in 1997 but prices weak.
newsitem.headline: More French property sales in 1997 but prices weak.

text.p: French property market experts said on Wednesday they expect property transaction volumes to rise to around 15 billion francs ($2.4 billion) this year, up from just over 10 billion last year, but that prices will remain weak.

"There is very good activity in the market for property investment, which is not matched by a recovery in prices," Emmanuel Schreder, partner and director for property investment at real estate consultancy and broker Auguste-Thouard, told Reuters.
The first half saw total sales of around nine billion francs, excluding sales by listed property companies, two leading French property specialists told Reuters.

Auguste-Thouard expects a market volume of about 15 billion francs for the year, including a huge sale at the Defense business district on the Paris outskirts worth 4.2 billion francs from Compagnie Generale d'Immobilier, the property arm of utilities group Generale des Eaux.
That annual total compares with more than 10 billion francs in 1996, around five billion in 1995 and an average 10-12 billion in the preceding years.
"We should reach about 15 billion this year," said Guillaume Cailloux, co-head of Greenwich Bourdais, a property advisory firm.

Cailloux attributes the increased volume to the need for liquidity among French asset holders, particularly the large insurance companies, such as Axa, Gan and AGF and renewed interest among foreign investors.
"I think we will see a terrific third quarter," he said, adding that several "large transactions" were being negotiated.

Auguste-Thouard's Schreder said the current deals concerned sales of small non-quoted property companies and portfolios of buildings, some of which are of the size of AGF's sale of 16 properties to the mutually-owned MAAF.

Insurer AGF said on Monday it sold 16 Paris properties for 850 million francs, totalling 45,000 square metres all situated between the Etoile and Opera districts in central Paris, comprising 18,000 of office space, 12,000 of commercial space, and 15,000 of residential space.
The sale generated 22 million francs in capital gains on the book value, it said.
